**Scope**: 5 projects (3 src, 2 test), no `Directory.Build.props/targets`, no Central Package Management.

---

## 🔴 Errors (Likely Broken or Will Cause Problems)

### 1. Package Version Skew — `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

| Project | Version |
|---|---|
| `ContosoApp.Core` | **8.0.0** |
| `ContosoApp.Services` | **8.0.1** |
| `ContosoApp.Api` | **8.0.0** |

`ContosoApp.Api` references both `Core` (8.0.0) and `Services` (8.0.1) transitively. NuGet will unify to 8.0.1 at restore, but the explicit 8.0.0 pin in `Core` and `Api` is misleading and fragile. If a future patch introduces a behavioral change, two projects will silently get a version they didn't declare. This is the #1 source of "works on my machine" diamond-dependency bugs.

**Fix**: Adopt Central Package Management (see §Suggestions below) or at minimum align all three to `8.0.1`.

### 2. Test Package Version Drift — Incompatible xunit Versions

| Package | `Api.Tests` | `Core.Tests` |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` | **17.9.0** | **17.10.0** |
| `xunit` | **2.7.1** | **2.8.1** |
| `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | **2.5.6** | **2.8.1** |

`xunit` 2.7→2.8 is a **minor version bump** with API surface changes. Running two test projects in the same CI pipeline with different xunit versions can cause runner compatibility issues (e.g., `xunit.runner.visualstudio` 2.5.6 is not validated against `xunit` 2.8.x). This drift will only worsen as more test projects are added.

**Fix**: Align all test packages to the same versions, ideally via Central Package Management.

---

## 🟡 Warnings (Anti-Patterns to Fix)

### 3. Massive Property Duplication Across All 5 Projects

Every single project repeats these 5 properties identically:

```xml
<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
```

And all 5 projects repeat:

```xml
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

That's **35 duplicated property lines** across the solution. This violates DRY and is a maintenance liability — if you upgrade to `net9.0`, you must edit 5 files instead of 1.

**Fix**: Extract to a root `Directory.Build.props` (see §Consolidated Fix below).

### 4. Duplicated Custom Target `PrintBuildInfo` in All 3 src Projects

All three `src/` projects contain an identical target:

```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
</Target>
```

Duplicated targets are a classic MSBuild anti-pattern. If you need to change the message format, you must edit 3 files. Worse, if someone adds a 4th project and forgets the target, behavior becomes inconsistent.

**Fix**: Move to `Directory.Build.targets` (targets with `BeforeTargets`/`AfterTargets` **must** go in `.targets`, not `.props`, because they depend on SDK-defined targets that aren't imported yet during `.props` evaluation).

### 5. Duplicated `DocumentationFile` Property in All 3 src Projects

```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

This is repeated in all `src/` projects but not in test projects — a perfect candidate for conditional extraction.

**Fix**: Move to `Directory.Build.props` with a condition excluding test projects (see below).

### 6. Split PropertyGroups in src Projects

Each src project has two `<PropertyGroup>` blocks with no condition differentiating them:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <!-- main properties -->
</PropertyGroup>
<!-- ... -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <DocumentationFile>...</DocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

Unconditionally split PropertyGroups reduce readability for no benefit.

**Fix**: Merge into a single `<PropertyGroup>` (or better, move `DocumentationFile` to `Directory.Build.props`).

### 7. `xunit.runner.visualstudio` Missing `PrivateAssets` / Runtime-Only Marker

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="..." />
```

This package is a test infrastructure dependency that should not flow to downstream consumers. While test projects are marked `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>` (which mitigates the risk), best practice is:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="..." PrivateAssets="all" />
```

This makes the intent explicit and protects against future refactoring where `IsPackable` might be removed.

### 8. `System.Text.Json` Declared Redundantly in `ContosoApp.Api`

`ContosoApp.Api` directly references `System.Text.Json` 8.0.5, but it also has a `ProjectReference` to `ContosoApp.Core` which already brings in the same package at the same version. Unless `Api` needs a *specific minimum version different from Core's*, this is redundant and creates another version-alignment obligation.

**Fix**: Remove the direct `System.Text.Json` reference from `Api` and let it flow transitively from `Core`.

---

## 🔵 Suggestions (Improvements for Maintainability)

### 9. Adopt Central Package Management (CPM)

With 5 projects and 9 distinct packages (several referenced in multiple projects), this solution is an ideal candidate for CPM. Create a `Directory.Packages.props` at the repo root:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Shared -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Swashbuckle.AspNetCore" Version="6.5.0" />
    <!-- Test -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.10.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Then each `.csproj` drops the `Version=` attribute:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit" />
```

This **eliminates version drift by construction** — the problems in §1 and §2 become impossible.

### 10. Create `Directory.Build.props` (Consolidated)

```xml
<!-- /Directory.Build.props -->
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- XML docs for non-test projects -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

This removes **~45 lines** of duplicated XML across 5 projects.

### 11. Create `Directory.Build.targets` (Consolidated)

```xml
<!-- /Directory.Build.targets -->
<Project>
  <!-- Only for src projects -->
  <Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build"
          Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
  </Target>
</Project>
```

### 12. Consider Adding a `global.json`

No `global.json` was found. For reproducible builds, pin the SDK version:

```json
{
  "sdk": {
    "version": "8.0.400",
    "rollForward": "latestPatch"
  }
}
```

This prevents CI/CD breakage when a new SDK ships with breaking analyzer rules (especially relevant since `TreatWarningsAsErrors` is enabled).
